gloss: rousing oneself; mustering energy; stirring to action

definitions.gloss: rousing oneself; mustering energy; stirring to action
definitions.explanation: summoning one's energy and determination to take action

examples.japanese: {奮起|ふんき}して{仕事|しごと}に{取|と}り{組|く}む。
examples.english: I rouse myself and tackle the work.

examples.japanese: チームの{奮起|ふんき}を{促|うなが}した。
examples.english: I urged the team to rouse themselves.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}を{糧|かて}に{奮起|ふんき}して、{再挑戦|さいちょうせん}することにした。
examples.english: I decided to learn from my failure, rouse myself, and try again.

notes:
{奮起|ふんき} means to muster energy and motivation, often after facing difficulties or setbacks.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
- {奮|ふん} (rouse, stir up)
- {起|き} (rise, get up)

USAGE:
- {奮起|ふんき}する (to rouse oneself - suru verb)
- {奮起|ふんき}を{促|うなが}す (to urge someone to rouse themselves)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {奮起|ふんき}して〜する (to rouse oneself and do ~)
- 〜に{奮起|ふんき}する (to be stirred to action by ~)

NUANCE:
- Implies gathering determination after setback or challenge
- Often used in sports, work, or personal development contexts
- Positive connotation of taking action

RELATED TERMS:
- {発奮|はっぷん} (being roused to action)
- {奮闘|ふんとう} (hard struggle)
- {奮|ふる}い{立|た}つ (to be stirred up)
- やる{気|き}を{出|だ}す (to get motivated - casual)
